title: Wall-vs-lumen sub-containment of high-density focus
instruction: Localize the high-density focus mask within the aorta. Determine whether it sits in {wall, lumen, surrounding_tissue}. State the pathology implied by that sub-location, choosing from {atherosclerosis, intraluminal embolus or thrombus, perivascular lymphadenopathy, phlebolith, normal variant} (typical mappings: wall calcification → atherosclerosis; luminal density → embolus/thrombus; perivascular → lymphadenopathy).

asset_grounding.notes: Anchored to M3D-RefSeg matched whitelist case s0146 (mask_label_count=5).

ground_truth.notes: v3 auto_seed: value + rationale derived deterministically from source mask_text; expert should verify and refine the evidence_slice / evidence_slices fields before release.
ground_truth.rationale: On CT, calcific foci (>=130 HU rim density) sitting at the muscular media of the aortic wall — not floating inside the contrast-filled lumen and not in the periaortic soft tissue — are the classic appearance of atherosclerotic plaque. Luminal high-density would suggest embolus / thrombus; perivascular nodes would be lymphadenopathy.

title: Pairwise mask-anatomy topology and clinical significance
instruction: This volume contains multiple labeled mask components. Consider the specific pair below: **Component A** = the high-density peritoneal nodule mask (the small focus on the upper-left peritoneal surface; corresponds to the metastasis-suspicious lesion). **Anatomy B** = the sigmoid colon wall (the closest bowel-wall structure to the nodule). Classify the spatial relation between A and B as one of {contains, contained_by, adjacent, disjoint}. State whether the observed relation is pathologically significant (one of {yes, incidental, no}) and justify on one rendered evidence view.

ground_truth.rationale: A peritoneal-seeding nodule sits on the serosal surface of the bowel — touching but not breaching the muscularis. Topologically that is 'adjacent' (shared surface, neither contains the other), not 'contains' or 'contained_by'. Clinical significance is 'yes' because peritoneal carcinomatosis = AJCC M1c (stage IV), regardless of whether the bowel wall is breached.

ground_truth.rationale: Serosal seeding does not invade through the bowel wall by definition — the implant grows on the outer surface rather than from the mucosa outward. Two orthogonal slice views should show continuous muscularis with no transmural defect. The stage is M1c (distant peritoneal metastasis) and is independent of whether bowel-wall invasion is also present.

ground_truth.rationale: A strip-like blurred high-density shadow described as 'suspected local infection' is the CT appearance of cellulitis. Necrotizing fasciitis / deep-compartment extension would require gas in the deep tissue, fluid tracking across the fascial plane, or stranding that bridges fascia — none of which are mentioned in the source caption. Therefore the inflammatory process is contained in the subcutaneous layer and does not breach into the femoral neurovascular bundle.
